evidence.quote:
She had never accustomed herself to those senseless
monosyllables that parodied her name; nor could she understand the frame
of mind that found them preferable to the comfortable "Aunt Jule" of the
old days.
evidence.paraphrase: Miss Trueman dislikes the fashionable nicknames her nieces use and prefers her old name.

evidence.quote:
Here were two points of view as little likely to coincide as the
parallel lines of science, and at some such stage as this the
discussions were wont to cease.
evidence.paraphrase: The narration frames the aunt's and nieces' outlooks as irreconcilably opposed.

evidence.quote:
The first six months of her sojourn had been almost entirely occupied
with accustoming herself to the absence of an attic and a cellar; long
days of depression they learned, finally, to trace to this incredible
source.
evidence.paraphrase: Aunt Julia struggled and became depressed adjusting to apartment life without an attic or cellar.

evidence.quote:
not only tallied so accurately with their digestive and aesthetic
necessities, but appeared, moreover, with such gratifying regularity one
hour later.
evidence.paraphrase: The nieces' Continental breakfast is contrasted with the aunt's hearty early-morning fare.

evidence.quote:
"And I tell you, Carrie, when you have cleaned house regularly, spring
and fall, for forty years, ever since you were born, it makes an awful
break to give it up!
evidence.paraphrase: Aunt Julia explains her attachment to her traditional domestic routines.

evidence.quote:
they saw upon her floured left hand an unmistakable shining
gold band.
evidence.paraphrase: The nieces discover their aunt has married, changing her situation.
